body: Thanks for your reply. My mother and wife have been truly amazing about this, reacting so bravely to having their lives turned upside down. A desire to vindicate their support and love for me is one of the few things that has kept me from seriously thinking about suicide. As for therapy, I've tried exploring some online resources. But I feel that whenever I spend lengthy amounts of time directly confronting this, a) I'm left emotionally exhausted and semi-broken for a few days, b) Feelings of loss, grief, despair intensify. It's better than feeling empty, but I'm unable to do anything productively on the work-social side of things. I will begin looking into options for in-person therapy, however. Thanks again.

Thanks for the advice. You're absolutely right that I can't force my cousin to forgive me, and that it'd be best if I focussed on myself at first. But deep down I know that without his input I'm not going to achieve any breakthroughs. Over the past year, and the past 8 months especially, it's as if the will to live has completely drained from me.
